beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: To compare two numbers, find which is greater, which is less, or that they are equal. A flat is one hundred.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Nine rods and nine squares make ninety-nine, the most the tens and ones can hold.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ninety-nine is less than one hundred.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which number is less? One hundred thirty-six or six hundred thirty-one.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Six hundred thirty-one is less. It ends in one, and one is small.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: That six is six ones: six small squares.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This six is six hundreds: six flats.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Start at the hundreds. One hundred is less than six hundreds.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The tens and ones make ninety-nine at most, so they cannot change that.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So one hundred thirty-six is less than six hundred thirty-one. It is the smaller number.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Less than means smaller. This sign is called less than: its open side faces the greater number.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Eight hundred ten, an empty square, eight hundred nine. Choose the symbol and the place-value reason.

do.text: $810\ \square\ 809$ Choose the symbol and the place-value reason.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Hundreds: eight and eight, the same. Tens: one and zero, not the same.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One ten is ten ones. All nine ones on the other side are still one short.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: So the ones cannot change it. Greater than means bigger: eight hundred ten is greater than eight hundred nine.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four hundred forty, an empty square, four hundreds, four tens and zero ones. Choose the symbol and the place-value reason.

do.text: $440\ \square$ 4 hundreds, 4 tens and 0 ones. Choose the symbol and the place-value reason.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Hundreds: four and four. Tens: four and four. Ones: zero and zero. Every place matches, so they are equal.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Equal means the same amount.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A hundred is more than all the tens and ones can make.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A ten is more than all the ones.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Start at the hundreds. The first place that is different decides.

do.text: The first place that is different decides.
